No comments or suggestions have been received from the general public in response to the notices published by the petitioner under Section 64 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (“the Act”). The petitioner has served the petition on the respondents. None of the respondents have filed any reply. Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **3** of **60** 4. The hearing in the matter was held on 25.10.2016. Having heard the representatives of the petitioner, respondents and perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the petition. c. The final transmission tariff for the part scope of the subject cited scheme (4 assets) i.e. except the assets covered under the present petition, for the tariff period 2009-14, was approved, vide order dated 2.12.2013 in Petition no. 102/TT/2012. The final tariff approved for the tariff period 2009-14, in Petition no. 102/TT/2012 was trued-up vide order dated 29.2.2016 in Petition No. 505/TT/2014; Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **7** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **8** of **60** “15. The Commission directed the petitioner to submit reasons along with documentary evidence for time over-run in commissioning of the instant assets. The petitioner vide affidavit dated 20.9.2013 submitted the actual COD of the instant assets and has submitted that the delay in the commissioning of the instant assets is due to the delay in supply and due to delay in construction of foundation work on account of unavoidable circumstances. However, the petitioner has not submitted any documentary evidence. Further, the petitioner vide affidavit dated 19.6.2014 submitted that additional RoE has not been claimed in the instant petition. We have considered the submissions made by the petitioner and the respondents. The petitioner has not submitted any documentary evidence justifying the time over-run. We are of the view that time over-run in case of these assets is on account of delay on the part of suppliers and the petitioner. As such, we are not inclined to condone the time over-run in the case of the instant assets.” Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **11** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **12** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **14** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **16** of **60** (9) In case of dispute, any of the parties may make an application in accordance with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 1999, as amended from time to time, including statutory reenactment thereof for settlement of the dispute: Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **17** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **18** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **19** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **21** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **23** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **24** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **27** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **31** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **32** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **33** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **34** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **36** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **37** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **39** of **60** Order in Petition No. 181/TT/2015 Page **41** of **60** other charges is exclusive of incentive, late payment surcharge, FERV, any statutory taxes, levies, duties, cess, or any other kind of impositions etc. The same, if imposed shall be borne and additionally paid by the respondents.
